Top Stock Market Highlights of the Week: StarHub, Singtel, Jurong Lake District and CrowdStrike
article:
Singapore’s telco sector took centre stage this week.
StarHub Ltd
(SGX: CC3) agreed to merge with M1, which is controlled by
Keppel Ltd
(SGX: BN4), while
Singapore Telecommunications Limited
(SGX: Z74), or Singtel, completed the transfer of its special discounted shares to holders’ own Central Depository (CDP) accounts on 21 November.
In property, a consortium that includes
Sing Holdings Limited
(SGX: 5IC) clinched a closely watched white site (a government land plot that can be developed for a flexible mix of homes, offices and shops) in Jurong Lake District on 24 November.
Over in the US,
CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc.
(NASDAQ: CRWD) agreed on 23 November to acquire
Zscaler, Inc.
(NASDAQ: ZS) in an all-stock deal that values Zscaler at about US$44 billion.
A three-player mobile market takes shape as StarHub moves for M1
StarHub has agreed to merge with M1
in an all-share deal valuing Keppel’s telco at about S$1.06 billion.
StarHub will issue around 651.7 million new shares, worth S$677.7 million, to M1’s shareholders and take on up to S$380 million of M1’s net debt, leaving Keppel with 23% of StarHub.
StarHub is also buying Circles Life’s Singapore mobile business, which has about 290,000 subscribers.
Both deals need regulatory approval and are expected to close in the first half of 2027 (1H 2027).
The merger would cut Singapore’s mobile network operators from four to three.
Bloomberg Intelligence data as at June 2026 shows M1 and StarHub together held about 43% of mobile subscribers, matching Singtel.
Incoming CEO Matt Williams said StarHub’s “intention is to keep things stable” on pricing in 2027, and analysts do not expect a meaningful recovery in revenue per user before late 2028.
On 24 November 2026, StarHub shares closed 3% higher at S$1.04, while Keppel’s fell 4.6% to S$8.42.
Singtel’s discounted shares move out of CPF Board’s hands after three decades
Singtel
and the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board have transferred 477 million Singtel special discounted shares (SDS) to the Central Depository (CDP) accounts of about 406,000 holders.
The transfer was completed on 21 November 2026.
The SDS were sold to CPF members at a discount in two tranches, during Singtel’s initial public offering in 1993 and again in 1996, with the CPF Board acting as trustee.
About 615,000 Singaporeans held SDS when the exercise began in April 2026. Around 34% of them, or 209,000 holders, sold their shares before the transfer.
With the CPF Board no longer their trustee, holders now own and manage their shares directly.
Sale proceeds remain exempt from CPF withdrawal conditions, and holders can keep them in their CPF Ordinary Account or withdraw them as cash.
Singtel group chief financial officer Arthur Lang said the exercise was “ultimately about giving SDS holders a choice”.
A record-setting land bid kicks off Jurong Lake District’s next chapter
On 24 November 2026, the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) awarded the white site at Town Hall Link in Jurong Lake District (JLD) to a consortium of CapitaLand Development, Far East Organization, Sino Group and Sing Holdings.
The winning bid of about S$1.82 billion, or around S$910 per square foot per plot ratio, was 38.9% above Sim Lian Group’s rival bid of S$1.31 billion.
Property consultants expect it to set a record for the highest land price by quantum for a white site outside the Central Area.
The 3.7-hectare, 99-year leasehold site links to the Jurong East MRT interchange and the future Cross Island Line station, and can yield about 1,200 homes, at least 40,000 square metres of office space and up to 44,000 square metres of retail space.
Sing Holdings will hold 15% of the residential and office components through a subsidiary. Ronald Tay, CEO of CapitaLand Development (Singapore & International), said the site “sits at the heart of JLD’s next phase of growth”.
A US$44 billion bet on cybersecurity in the AI era
CrowdStrike
will acquire cloud security company Zscaler in an all-stock deal worth about US$43.9 billion, the companies announced on 23 November 2026.
Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each share they own, a 34% premium to Zscaler’s closing price on 20 November 2026.
Existing CrowdStrike shareholders will own about 84.1% of the combined company, with Zscaler shareholders holding the remaining 15.9%.
The deal pairs CrowdStrike’s endpoint security for devices such as laptops with Zscaler’s cloud-based network protection.
The firms already share about 2,000 customers through a partnership, and expect the combination to expand their market by more than US$185 billion by 2029.
Noting that security once meant keeping attackers out, CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said: “Today, safety is required to let AI in.”
CrowdStrike shares fell more than 7% in pre-market trading on 23 November 2026, while Zscaler’s rose 20%.
The deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike’s fiscal year 2028, which begins in February 2027.

title: Smart Look At The Week Ahead: RBI, Salesforce, Docusign And Macy’s
article:
Only one major central bank is set to announce interest rates next week. The Reserve Bank of India is expected to raise the repo rate from 5.5% to 5.75%. A rise in energy prices has pushed the inflation rate above the bank’s target band of 2% and 6%.
The RBI doesn’t need to wait for the Fed to move first. A rate hike by the US central bank in December is a nailed-on certainty. Additionally, with India’s economic growth expected to be robust, the RBI has enough leeway to move.
Aside from economic issues, Jensen Huang, who was reinstated as CEO of NVIDIA, will testify before Congress. He is expected to answer questions about the company’s ties to Singapore-based Megaspeed and NVIDIA’s business in China.
On the corporate front
Salesforce
(NYSE: CRM) does not believe that AI will disrupt its business. In fact, it is engaging AI to strengthen its business. It will integrate Anthropic’s Claude AI models into its products such as Slack and Agentforce. Salesforce could report high single-digit growth in revenue for the third quarter.
Docusign
(Nasdaq: DOCU) has also  embraced AI to improve customer experience. Its AI assistant can analyse agreement terms, reviews and generate contracts. The E-signature platform is expected to report a strong increase in earnings per share.
Macy’s
(NYSE: M) is nearing the end of a turnaround strategy to revitalise its store locations. The market will be looking to see if the department store can continue. In the second quarter, Macy’s said that growth has been driven by its reimagined stores. At that time, it raised its full-year guidance for both revenue and earnings per share.
Ulta Beauty
(Nasdaq: ULTA) is expected to announce another set of strong number for the quarter. Earnings could be almost 10% higher, whilst revenue could be up by 5%. The beauty-shop chain has invested in customer loyalty by personalising its promotional strategies. It has also continued to invest in mobile-app engagement and social media to fuel E-commerce growth.

title: US stocks rebound as traders pile into battered tech shares
article:
(Nov 27): US stocks rallied Friday, capping a week of whiplash as dip buyers scooped up some beaten down technology shares despite lingering worries about the sustainability of the artificial-intelligence boom.

The S&P 500 Index advanced 1.6%, while the Nasdaq 100 Index soared 2.6% after US markets reopened from Thursday’s holiday. Trading ended early at 1pm in New York on Friday.

Stocks have swung sharply this week, with Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia’s chief executive officer and Anthropic PBC’s brief fall below its IPO price adding to volatility across the AI trade. Anthropic jumped 11% Friday. A key gauge of market turbulence — the Cboe Volatility Index, or VIX — was near 24 after briefly spiking to nearly 35 on Wednesday, when markets tumbled early in the session before clawing back the losses.

The advance gave traders a reprieve from selloffs that have pulled the S&P 500 down nearly 7% from its Oct 6 record and send the Nasdaq 100 down 14%.

Nvidia Corp rose nearly 1%, erasing earlier losses. A gauge of chip stocks rebounded along with other AI beneficiaries, including data-storage firm SanDisk Corp., which soared 16%, and Micron Technology Inc, which gained nearly 8%. Optical-products maker Lumentum Holdings Inc and server maker Dell Technologies Inc gained 8% and 6.7%, respectively.

The advance left the S&P 500 notching its best week since April 2025 with a 5.6% gain, while Nasdaq 100’s nearly 7% rally this week was its best since May 2025. The most speculative corners of the market were higher Friday, with Goldman Sachs Group Inc’s basket of the most-shorted stocks rising 2.6% — with its 8.1% weekly gain its best since August — while a basket of unprofitable tech companies jumped 4% on Friday.

See also: Nasdaq 100 tumbles as Nvidia euphoria fades, new tariffs floated

Thinner-than-normal liquidity in a holiday-shortened week amplified volatility, with volume roughly 10% below its average for the S&P 500 compared with the past 30 days, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

“Despite any rebounds, this is the most nervous half day of trading for investors that we’ve seen in years, given that there’s not a lot of conviction around Nvidia still,” said JJ Kinahan, senior vice president, head of retail expansion and alternative investment products at Cboe Global Markets.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave Inc rose 3.7%, while Nebius Group NV rose 5.3%. AI hyperscalers Meta Platforms Inc rallied more than 3% while Amazon.com Inc jumped 4%. Apple Inc rose nearly 1%. Oracle Corp advanced 3.1%. A basket of Magnificent Seven stocks rose 2.3%, notching its best week since April at 8.1%.

See also: Forced buying aided biggest rally since April 2025, says Nomura

Even with the advance, the S&P 500 is eyeing its worst November since the height of the 2008 financial crisis as the market is dragged down by concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom, elevated inflation and expectations that the Federal Reserve will resume raising interest rates next month.

Swap traders are almost fully pricing in a quarter-point rate hike in December after data this week showed the US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter and inflation accelerated in October.

“There’s still fierce debate over whether the AI trade is over or not,” said Michael Antonelli, market strategist at Baird. “Institutions will have to make decisions in the next few weeks over how to move forward and that will set the tone heading into 2027.”

US President Donald Trump has also sowed uncertainty with tariff hikes planned on imports from China, Japan, the European Union and other trading partners. Key events to watch next week include Huang’s congressional testimony following his reinstatement at Nvidia and the November US jobs report.

Traders remained optimistic Friday, though, as strong profit outlooks during the crucial holiday season would present a much-needed tailwind. Estimates from the National Retail Federation imply a 4.2% growth in holiday retail sales in 2026 from a year ago, compared with 3.1% in 2025. On Black Friday alone, Americans are expected to spend almost US$13 billion ($16.8 billion) in online transactions, data from Adobe Analytics shows.

So far, earnings results from retail companies have been mixed. Earlier this week, Dollar Tree Inc’s third-quarter adjusted earnings per share and comparable sales topped Wall Street expectations, while Best Buy Co Inc raised its guidance for the year on resilient demand for computing. Target Corp’s sales beat estimates, while TJX Companies Inc narrowed its earnings outlook.

More retailers will report earnings next week, including Macy’s Inc and Dollar General Corp.

On Friday, defensive stocks that tend to have comparatively low valuations and offer robust dividends were slipping after outperforming earlier in the week, with Coca-Cola Co, Procter & Gamble Co and JM Smucker Co all closing lower.

Investors had flocked to such consumer staples companies in the past few months, putting them on track for the best quarter since 2000. The advance has made valuations look stretched: the S&P 500 Consumer Staples Index is sitting at 24 times projected earnings, the most since the 1990s.
